{"R1": {"R1P1": {"snippet_ids": ["S1", "S5"], "text": "The commercial operations snapshot reports contract outcomes, not a customer-level retention rate. It does not state the number of distinct enterprise customers represented by the twelve expiring contracts or the number of those customers retained. It also does not provide an approved definition for customer retention.

At the start of the quarter Maple had twelve enterprise contracts scheduled to expire during the quarter. By the close of the quarter, the account team had recorded eight of those contracts as renewed and two as not renewed. The remaining two were still being negotiated and had not been assigned a final outcome.", "status": "unknown"}, "R1P2": {"snippet_ids": ["S3", "S4", "S5", "S6"], "text": "An account manager contacts each enterprise customer before contract expiry and documents the customer's decision in the renewal tracker. The finance team validates the commercial terms before a renewal is marked complete. Negotiations can continue beyond the nominal expiry date if both parties agree.

A renewal record includes the contract identifier and its outcome. The process note does not define a customer retention metric or how customers with multiple contracts should be counted.

At the start of the quarter Maple had twelve enterprise contracts scheduled to expire during the quarter. By the close of the quarter, the account team had recorded eight of those contracts as renewed and two as not renewed. The remaining two were still being negotiated and had not been assigned a final outcome.

The count refers to contracts rather than individual customer organizations. A customer can have more than one enterprise contract.", "status": "unknown"}}}
